study: Durable runtime throughput under synthetic finite load

units.worker: independently verified Python tool tasks/active second
units.admission: independently verified ordinary input settlements/active second

contract.aggregation: two trials per revision and cell; preserve every failure; report range and median without pooling latency quantiles
contract.qualification: finite same-machine synthetic comparison; no production SLO, throughput rating, confidence interval or live inference measurement

methodology.worker: one outstanding external input/session; actual python_exec, observed terminal, committed follow-up, exact marker check
methodology.admission: aggregate absolute-rate ordinary inputs; real batching; no rejection retries; accepted-input drain
methodology.durability: runtime defaults: FULL activation/snapshot/receipt and effect commits; asynchronous observation journal
methodology.latency_clock: asyncio loop monotonic seconds; latency distributions in milliseconds
methodology.percentiles: nearest rank; samples counts included; null when empty
methodology.rate_denominator: active seconds including warm-worker execution and accepted drain; excludes startup, warm-up, shutdown and offline checks
methodology.cpu: parent process only; worker process CPU excluded
methodology.lag: 10 ms absolute timer; skipped missed timer deadlines; final overdue deadline sampled
methodology.failure_counts: failed includes explicit errors or unverified settled work; unfinished means no completion settlement; counts can overlap
methodology.goodput_integrity: only accepted jobs with independent evidence in sessions passing exact-set/row/event/journal checks contribute goodput
methodology.limits: finite synthetic scripts; retained listener events and ScriptedBackend request history add overhead; no user workload or latency SLO supplied
